title: Transnasal stimulation & depth-resolved neural recording
summary: Developed an in vivo mouse platform combining a 32-site nasal stimulation array and 64-channel intracerebral recordings to characterize stimulation-evoked activity across recording depths. Current work examines response timing, stimulation parameters, and anatomical correspondence—not yet selective deep-brain activation.
contribution: Designed and integrated a preclinical stimulation–recording workflow, including nasal electrode configurations, stereotaxic neural recordings, data quality controls, and analysis tools.
outcome: Recorded depth-resolved stimulation-evoked activity across the mouse brain. Observed short-latency responses in deep recording channels; the degree of anatomical targeting and selectivity remains under investigation.

title: Why electric-field orientation matters
summary: Designed orthogonal stimulation configurations for cortical brain slices and paired neural recordings with FEM modeling. Observed activation thresholds more than fivefold lower for out-of-plane fields than for fields aligned with cortical columns.
contribution: Built and validated ex vivo measurement configurations, acquired electrophysiology data, and investigated the relation between field direction and activation threshold.
outcome: Published evidence that field orientation relative to tissue structure can strongly influence neural activation in this ex vivo model.

title: Scalable EEG platforms for zebrafish
summary: Built multi-animal EEG systems for adult and larval zebrafish using mechanical design and microfluidics. Validated recording performance in seizure and anti-epileptic treatment models. Related device inventions received registrations in Korea and the EU.
contribution: Designed device architectures and recording workflows for repeatable multi-animal EEG studies, including microfluidic positioning for larval zebrafish.
outcome: Published EEG platforms for adult and larval zebrafish and contributed to registered EEG device patents in Korea and the EU.

title: Connecting electric-field models with physiology
summary: Use FEM simulations, electrode configurations, and experimental response measurements to reason about stimulation efficacy and model limitations. Contributed to preclinical evaluation of transnasal DeepFocus stimulation.
contribution: Developed and interpreted computational electric-field models, compared candidate electrode configurations, and connected predicted fields to electrophysiology questions.
outcome: Contributed to conference and collaborative work investigating the feasibility and limitations of transnasal brain stimulation.
